strategy.sub_strategy: Korean equity long-short pairs trading and event-driven
strategy.description: ANDA Long-Short Dream seeks to generate consistently superior risk-adjusted returns with relatively low volatility through a multi-strategy equity focus expressed through three to four core strategies: pair trades (dominant at ~92–98% of gross exposure), index rebalancing, and event driven (IPOs, rights issues, appraisal rights, tender offers, merger/split arbitrage). Pair trades include three types: preferred/common share pairs (exploiting structural undervaluation of preferred shares in Korea due to corporate governance issues), holding/subsidiary company pairs (exploiting double-counting discount in Korean holding companies), and intra-sector pairs (style rotation and asymmetrical short-selling using KOSPI200 and KOSDAQ150 constituents). Index rebalancing strategy exploits passive flow from ETF/index rebalancing (KOSPI200, KOSDAQ150, MSCI) by entering positions on stocks forecasted for index addition in advance. Capital allocation is dynamic based on best market opportunities. Following a Summer 2023 drawdown of -11.4%, the PM introduced enhanced risk controls targeting annual volatility ≤10%, top 3 pairs annual vol contribution ≤600bps, and max drawdown target ≤6%.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits structural and behavioral anomalies unique to the Korean equity market: preferred/common share price discrepancies driven by poor corporate governance, holding company NAV discounts from Korea's high dual-listing ratio (18% vs Japan 4.4%), and intra-sector pairs using proprietary statistical models including regression, GARCH, and PCA to identify mispricings between fundamentally related stocks. Targets uncorrelated returns in a market characterized by persistent governance discounts and frequent corporate actions.
strategy.idea_generation: Proprietary quantitative screening combining return correlation analysis, analyst reports, and business report data for universe construction; price spread monitoring flagging pairs deviating beyond ±2 standard deviations; fundamental and sentiment overlay assessing whether spread divergence is temporary before taking mean-reversion positions. Index rebalancing uses price and turnover data from May–October to forecast December additions, entering positions from July onwards.

strategy.sub_strategy: Fundamental long/short equity focused on financial services sector
strategy.description: Azora Capital employs a fundamental long/short equity strategy exclusively focused on the financial services sector, covering approximately 470 companies with ~150 under active coverage. The strategy exploits structural complexity, regulatory evolution, and behavioral inefficiencies in global financial services, including banks, asset managers, brokers & exchanges, fintech, insurance, specialty finance & mortgage, and real estate. Idea generation uses a systematic 13-week research cycle combining bottom-up stock selection, quarterly management contact, sell-side and buy-side crosschecks, and ongoing macroeconomic data monitoring. The portfolio is constructed bottom-up with 25-50 long positions and 30-50 short positions; typical gross exposure 150-250% and net exposure -10% to +30%. The strategy emphasizes single-name alpha shorts (avoiding ETF/basket hedges), subsector tilts up to +/-10% net, and focuses on liquid mid-to-large-cap financials. Significant emphasis on the short side of the portfolio with single-name 'alpha' shorts contributing materially to ITD returns. 81% of ITD total portfolio gross return attributed to alpha/asset selection per MSFS factor decomposition.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Financials present a structural investing moat due to their complex levered balance sheets, highly specific and evolving regulation, varied idiosyncratic subsectors, and cyclical/macroeconomic influences. Deep sector specialization and a broad active coverage model allow Azora to identify inflection points earlier than generalists, exploit mispricing in both directions, and generate consistent alpha from both longs and shorts across market cycles.
strategy.idea_generation: Ideas generated through a systematic 13-week quarterly research cycle: post-earnings follow-up (weeks 0-2), formal company communication (weeks 2-6), buy-side/sell-side crosscheck (weeks 7-8), intensive modeling and earnings prep (weeks 9-10), and processing earnings reports (weeks 11-13). Ongoing monitoring of macroeconomic data (FED H8, master trust credit, exchange trading volumes, asset manager flows). Universe of ~470-500 names, with active coverage of ~150. CIO makes final investment and sizing decisions after collaborative team discussion. Investment ideas ranked on risk/reward skew, market sentiment, short interest, and liquidity.

strategy.description: Market-neutral, rules-based long/short European equity strategy targeting approximately 1,500 listed European stocks, focused on the €3–15bn market cap range with ~70–80% Eurozone and ~20–30% Sweden. The stated alpha source is structured analysis of underutilised corporate disclosures, regulatory filings, and legal frameworks overlooked by mainstream analysts, combined with analyst estimate data, short interest, crowding signals, price/volume action, and credit market context. The process flows through four stages: systematic Idea Generation (screening of regulatory and legal filings), Diligence (binary risk/reward assessment), Investment Selection & Sizing (risk- and liquidity-driven, equal notional, no conviction trades), and Position Monitoring & Exit (daily re-underwriting; 17 defined exit criteria). Portfolio targets ~200 positions (80–100 per leg), with gross exposure of 180–200% unlevered and net exposure managed at 0 to ±10%. All decisions are ultimately discretionary but framed as systematic and rules-based. The long-only UCITS fund (Fundamental Select) is live since November 2024 and serves as the live long leg; the short book is tracked and logged daily with a named third party.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits information asymmetries in underutilised European corporate, regulatory, and legal filings — sources systematically overlooked by mainstream equity analysts — to identify operational trajectories before they are broadly priced in, generating idiosyncratic alpha on both long and short sides.
strategy.idea_generation: Systematic screening of 1,500 European listed companies using proprietary data scraping and processing of regulatory, legal, and corporate filings. Process is Bayesian, starting with tens of thousands of data points filtered to ~2% through custom datasets. Five external data suppliers (Reuters, Bloomberg, FactSet, and others) provide categorised feeds. Signal capture is fully automated with manual audits every few weeks. Drawing on operational experience in corporate banking and M&A to interpret filing signals. Roughly 80% of PM time is spent on research.

strategy.description: Meson Gravity is a fully systematic, market-neutral, sector-neutral, and factor-neutral equity statistical-arbitrage strategy focused on US small- and mid-cap equities (75% below S&P 500 market cap, minimum $150m). The system transforms point-in-time Capital IQ fundamentals and SEC filings into 3,000+ engineered features, then trains 300–500 specialized ML models (boosted gradient trees, non-linear ensembles) on a fixed 2007–2017 window, leaving 2018 onward as out-of-sample. A solver/optimizer layer dynamically weights model predictions, neutralizes market, sector, country and style-factor exposures, and constructs a portfolio of ~1,500–2,000 positions (750–1,000 longs and shorts). The strategy targets ~20%+ net annualized returns, Sharpe 2+, and maximum drawdowns below 10%, with ~5-week median holding period and weekly rebalancing.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Exploits systematic fundamental mispricing in less-competitive SMID-cap equities by applying deep ML-driven signal generation on point-in-time fundamental data, monetizing the persistent gap between economic gravity (intrinsic business value) and temporarily distorted market prices driven by sentiment, speculation, or episodic deleveraging.
strategy.idea_generation: Fully automated: raw fundamental data (Capital IQ point-in-time, EDGAR filings, analyst revision datasets) processed into 3,000+ engineered features; 300–500 specialized ML models generate stock rankings; solver layer synthesizes 12 ensembling techniques to produce combined predictions; optimizer enforces factor/sector neutrality and position constraints.

strategy.sub_strategy: Agency MBS derivatives – prepayment risk relative value (IO, IIO, PO)
strategy.description: Discretionary relative value strategy focused on structured Agency MBS derivatives, primarily Interest Only (IO), Inverse Interest Only (IIO), and Principal Only (PO) securities, with small tactical allocations to RMBS credit (CRT, Non-Agency IO) and consumer ABS (student loans, home equity) up to 25% of AUM. The strategy seeks to harvest hedge-adjusted interest income and exploit pricing inefficiencies in Agency mortgage prepayment risk while hedging out interest rate, curve, and volatility exposures using TBA contracts, Treasury futures, SOFR swaps, swaptions, and specified pools. Portfolio A targets a market-neutral interest rate posture but may carry residual duration of +/- 8 years based on macro views. Macro analysis drives broad sector allocation (IO vs IIO vs PO); bottom-up OAS modelling and loan-level prepayment analysis drive security selection. Core edge is multi-decade prepayment modelling expertise, CMO structuring capability, and MSR/whole-loan operating experience from the predecessor Laurel Road and West Side Advisors platforms.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Agency MBS prepayment risk is systematically underpriced relative to corporate credit and other spread products, particularly in lock-in environments where >85% of borrowers hold below-market note rates, creating abnormally low prepayment speeds that models fail to fully capture. Exploits pricing inefficiencies and wide spreads in Agency MBS derivatives by harvesting hedge-adjusted carry where specialized prepayment modeling expertise provides an informational edge over generalist fixed income managers.
strategy.idea_generation: Top-down macro analysis sets interest rate and prepayment outlook, informing sector weights across IO, IIO, and PO. Bottom-up OAS modelling via YieldBook, JPMorgan MSC, and Bloomberg BAM, combined with proprietary prepayment models and loan-level surveillance (CPR/CDR, FNMA/FHLMC/GNMA data), screens for securities with attractive yield-to-forward and robust stress performance. New-issue CMO creation monitoring provides additional alpha source when dealer structuring of IOs/IIOs is cheaper than secondary market.
strategy.neutrality_approach: Dollar and duration neutral (target zero net DV01); manages to near-zero net interest rate exposure with residual duration bias of +/- 8 years based on short-term view
strategy.family_defining_note: Absolute return, uncorrelated to equities and traditional fixed income; no formal benchmark. Predecessor WAF fund showed correlations of 14% to S&P 500, 7% to Bloomberg US Agg, and 23% to HFRI Composite.

market_views.macro_thesis: RichBrook expects a gradual Fed cutting cycle in 2026 with rates remaining range-bound in H1 2025 before further easing in H2. Base case anticipates yield curve steepening driven by lower front-end rates (Fed cuts) and higher long-end rates (fiscal/deficit concerns), which benefits Agency derivatives—particularly IIO whose coupon resets inversely to 1-month SOFR. Prepayment risk remains low as >85% of borrowers hold mortgage rates 300+ bp below prevailing levels. Agency MBS spreads remain historically wide relative to Treasuries and corporates, providing attractive entry points. Most mortgage borrowers (90%+) are locked in at low rates and out of the money to refinance. The Fed is expected to continue running off its MBS portfolio and replace with US Treasuries.
sector_views: Agency IO (low WAC): Stable carry at 6-8% unlevered (10-11% with one turn of leverage); minimal prepayment risk; richly priced after tightening but still attractive on risk-adjusted basis.

Agency Inverse IO (high strike, prepay-sensitive): Wide OAS (600-1000bp Yield Book), high option value into a curve steepening/cutting cycle; 25%+ TROR potential in recession scenarios. IIO exposure on newer origination loans (2023+) expected to benefit from borrower burnout as fast prepayers refinance.
Agency IIO (low WAC, call-protected): Insurance against recessionary rate declines; OAS ~250bp; isolated SOFR sensitivity without prepayment risk. Creation of IIO derivatives has pushed spreads wide.
Non-Agency Jumbo IO: Provides carry premium to Agency IO with low WAC and jumbo loan-size protecting prepayments; monitoring liquidity concession.
Agency MBS (TBA): Historically wide spreads offer attractive hedge + carry; lower coupon positive convexity preferred over current coupon.

Home Equity (HELOC/second lien): Double-digit unlevered returns in aggregation with 3-4 pts securitization upside; GSE-underwritten borrowers with low combined LTVs. HELOC and CES securitization volume expected to reach $35bn+ in 2026 vs $29bn in 2025.
MSR: High single digit/low double digit levered net returns; 200-300bp premium to liquid Agency IO; capacity concerns limiting further additions.
geographic_views: US only; no non-US exposure permitted under current investment guidelines.
key_risks_identified: Prepayment spike risk if mortgage rates decline materially (>100bp from current levels); particularly acute for high-WAC IIO.
Model risk: OAS prepayment models may overstate/understate prepayment speeds in unprecedented rate environments; overreliance may cause inaccurate hedge ratios.
Funding/repo risk: balance sheet constraints at year-end and quarter-end can widen bid/offer spreads and increase haircuts.
GSE reform: privatization of Fannie/Freddie could disrupt Agency MBS market liquidity and spread dynamics.
IIO supply pressure: record CMO issuance driven by floater demand creating OAS widening in prepayment-sensitive sectors.
Long duration positioning subject to mark-to-market losses in higher rate scenarios.
Yield curve steepening via Fed rate cuts fails to materialize, potentially resulting in muted or negative performance.
Absence of a full performance record through 2021 (worst year on record for Agency managers; peer index -8.5%) limits ability to gauge potential drawdown in adverse conditions.
market_views.forward_outlook: RichBrook base case for 2026 targets 17.3% net return driven by IIO carry and price appreciation into further Fed cuts, stable IO carry, and continued mortgage basis tightening. Key upside scenario is mild recession (24.2% net) where IIO coupons surge and IO cashflows extend. Downside risk is inflationary no-landing scenario (3.4% net) where front-end rates rise and IIO prices decline. Mortgage spreads at historically wide levels are expected to provide attractive risk-adjusted carry. Initial portfolio expected to be approximately 60% IO and 40% IIO on a market value basis.

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: Risk management begins with understanding downside risks before any investment. Portfolio construction emphasizes diversification of underlying drivers of risk and return rather than simply increasing position count. Hard position limits: long positions 3–15% NAV (top conviction up to 15%), short positions typically below 2% NAV. Sector and factor concentration actively managed; exposure to any single macro factor restricted in number and size. Real-time monitoring of long book beta (typically ~0.7x vs MSCI Nordic) and short book beta (typically ~1.2–1.4x). Beta-adjusted net exposure kept around 50% despite 80–100% net long bias. For each position, a 'what if we are wrong' downside valuation is performed. Soft-close capacity limit set at USD 300m to preserve opportunity set.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: No pre-set mechanical drawdown trigger. In periods of volatility the team re-underwrites every position stress-testing fundamental prospects; exits opportunistic or shorter-term positions where risks are no longer compensated; increases concentration in highest-conviction core holdings. Active position sizing adjustments during volatile periods (e.g., April 2025: ~30% portfolio turnover in one month).

strategy.sub_strategy: Diversified Macro CTA with 75% trend-following and 25% diversifying signals
strategy.description: Winton's flagship CTA offering combining a core 75% trend-following allocation with 25% diversifying signals (carry, mean-reversion, seasonality, cross-sector macro relationships, fundamental models, and futures market dynamics) applied to 240+ macro markets including major and alternative markets. Trend following blends multiple speeds with a non-linear response function and inverse volatility weighting to counteract trend exhaustion. The strategy targets portfolio diversification and industry outperformance with no directional bias in equities and bonds. Risk allocation spans fixed income (19%), currencies (20%), energies (19%), agriculture (13%), metals (16%), equity indices (10%), credit (2%), industrials (1%), and digital assets (1%). Sector and market weights are optimised using hierarchical clustering for maximum diversification. Volatility target approximately 10% annualized.
strategy.investment_thesis_core: Profitable investment opportunities can be identified through systematic application of advanced statistical and pattern recognition techniques to large datasets. Trends persist due to human behavioural biases and crowd psychology; combining slow trend-following with diversifying macro signals produces higher Sharpe ratios and positive convexity during periods of stress for traditional 60/40 portfolios.
strategy.idea_generation: Fully systematic. Research projects prioritised by CIO based on return potential, feasibility, and strategic objectives. Daily portfolio construction combines signal generation, target positions, pre-trade monitoring, order management, and post-trade monitoring. All hypotheses pre-registered to mitigate analytical bias; peer review at multiple stages. Signals derived from price data, volume, open interest, spread relationships, momentum oscillators, seasonal and cyclical analysis, and certain fundamental/economic variables.
strategy.family_defining_note: Diversified Macro Strategy is a direct evolution of the historical Winton Diversified Program / Winton Futures Fund, retaining the core systematic CTA architecture with expanded diversifying signal set and broader market universe (240+ vs. 142 historical markets).

risk_framework.risk_framework_description: Multi-layered risk framework monitoring normal and extreme conditions. Normal: forecast volatility, realised volatility, betas to factors. Extreme: net and gross leverage, margin-to-equity, historical stress test, volatility-based stress test, correlation-based stress test. Hard limits include: no more than 10% of NAV as initial margin in any single market; no more than 50% of NAV as total initial margin. Pre-order hard limits, order generation limits, execution broker limits, and post-execution limits (margin-to-equity max 50% overall / 10% per single market, VaR at 95% 1-day, notional-to-equity, position/volume vs. exchange open interest, real-time P&L). Risk Manager proprietary system generates daily alert reports at 85% of limits. Volatility estimates are designed to be less sensitive to short-term changes; effect of diversification disappearing is monitored through time; strategies employ judicious leverage designed to avoid rapid rebalancing. Independent Risk Management Function (second line) reports to CCO separately from portfolio management.
risk_framework.drawdown_response_protocol: CIO and risk team may proactively reduce leverage when forward-looking stress tests and crowding metrics indicate elevated risk, even if model-implied volatility is within normal ranges. Decisions are consensus-driven and typically reduce volatility to the lower end of the operating range. No traditional stop-losses; risk controlled by daily systematic volatility forecasting and portfolio rebalancing. System development continues at all times but not in response to drawdown. Manual intervention permitted only to reduce risk during exceptional market events.
risk_framework.position_limits: No more than 10% of NAV committed as margin for any single market; no more than 50% of NAV committed to clearing brokers as initial margin.
risk_framework.sector_limits: Soft limits on sector margin-to-equity set in proprietary Risk Manager tool; sector-specific market execution limits agreed by Trading System Committee.
risk_framework.stop_loss_policy: No traditional stop-losses or profit targets; risk controlled by daily systematic volatility forecasting, portfolio rebalancing, and position closure when trend reverses.
risk_framework.risk_model_used: Proprietary daily volatility forecasting model at individual market level; covariance matrix for portfolio construction; margin-to-equity and VaR monitored daily.
